L00001: # MLAgentBench: Evaluating Language Agents on Machine Learning Experimentation
L00002: 
L00003: MLAgentBench is a suite of end-to-end Machine Learning (ML) experimentation tasks for benchmarking AI agents, where the agent aims to take a given 
L00004: dataset and a machine learning task description and autonomously develop or improve an ML model. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.03302
L00005: ![](figs/main.png)
L00006: 
L00007: Our AI agent in action on MLAgentBench:
L00008: [![Watch the video](https://img.youtube.com/vi/s9NANrjLEZs/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/s9NANrjLEZs)
L00009: 
L00010: Each task is an interactive environment that directly resembles what human researchers see,
L00011: where an agent can read available files, run multiple experiments on a compute cluster, and analyze results to achieve the specified research goal. 
L00012: Specifically, we include 13 diverse ML engineering tasks,
L00013: achievable by trying different machine learning methods, data processing, architectures, training processes, etc:
L00014: ![](figs/table.png)
L00015: 
L00016: 
L00017: # Setup
L00018: 
L00019: The MLAgentBench package can be installed with
L00020: ```
L00021: pip install -e .
L00022: ```
L00023: 
L00024: Install dependencies with python 3.10 by running 
L00025: ```
L00026: bash install.sh
L00027: ```
L00028: or use our [docker image](https://hub.docker.com/layers/qhwang123/researchassistant/latest/images/sha256-6b3690a13ba44fd089086e9860a298ed49a179d9a04a5406c0df074569a3aabe?context=repo). Since agent will modify and execute files, we recommend running experiments within sandboxes such as docker container.
L00029: For docker, use the following instructions: 
L00030: 1. Pull the docker image:
L00031: ```
L00032: docker pull qhwang123/researchassistant:latest
L00033: ```
L00034: 2. Run the docker container from the image, mounting the current directory to `/MLAgentBench` inside the container with root user permissions to install other packages:
L00035: - On Windows PowerShell
L00036: ```
L00037: docker run -it --user root -v ${PWD}:/MLAgentBench -w /MLAgentBench qhwang123/researchassistant:latest
L00038: ```
L00039: - On Mac or Linux
L00040: ```
L00041: docker run -it --user root -v "$(pwd)":/MLAgentBench -w /MLAgentBench qhwang123/researchassistant:latest
L00042: ```
L00043: 
L00044: Each dataset will be prepared when it is run the first time. You can also prepare them beforehand with 
L00045: ```
L00046: python -u -m MLAgentBench.prepare_task <task_name> $(which python)
L00047: ```
L00048: For Kaggle datasets, you need to set up Kaggle API and authentication (~/.kaggle/kaggle.json) as described [here](https://www.kaggle.com/docs/api). You may also need to provide manual consent to the rules of specific competitions by following the prompts. For docker, use the following instructions:
L00049: 1. Ensure that you have ".kaggle/kaggle.json" with your API credentials in the MLAgentBench root folder.
L00050: 2. Once your container is mounted (instructions above), run
L00051: ```
L00052: export KAGGLE_CONFIG_DIR=/MLAgentBench/.kaggle
L00053: pip install kaggle
L00054: sudo apt-get install unzip
L00055: ```
L00056: 
L00057: Finally, put API keys under the root directory of this repo (or wherever you run scripts from). Currently, we support OpenAI (openai_api_key.txt in the format of organization:APIkey), Claude (claude_api_key.txt), and CRFM API (crfm_api_key.txt). To use an AutoGPT agent, setup the directory as described [here](https://docs.agpt.co/setup/).
L00058: 
L00059: Update: We support gemini pro and huggingface now! To run gemini, fill in PROJECT_ID in LLM.py to your project id. To run huggingface, specifiy model as huggingface/<org name>/<model name>.
L00060: 
L00061: # Quick Start
L00062: 
L00063: To run our research agent on cifar10 task with openai API using gpt-4 and gpt-3.5-turbo:
L00064: 
L00065: ```
L00066: python -u -m MLAgentBench.runner --python $(which python) --task cifar10 --device 0 --log-dir first_test  --work-dir workspace --llm-name gpt-4 --edit-script-llm-name gpt-4 --fast-llm-name gpt-3.5-turbo >  first_test/log 2>&1
L00067: ```
L00068: 
L00069: Note: capturing log is necessary for oom error etc runtime error detection.
L00070: 
L00071: This will produce logs in `first_test` directory with the following structure
L00072: ```
L00073: first_test/
L00074:     agent_log/
L00075:         main_log # main log showing agent's research process
L00076:         agent_*.json # saved agent states
L00077:         ...
L00078:     env_log/
L00079:         tool_logs/ 
L00080:         traces/ # snap shots of the agent workspace
L00081:         trace.json # interaction trace of the agent
L00082:         overall_time.txt # overall time
L00083:         error.txt # will be generated if there is a system error
L00084: ```
L00085: 
L00086: If llm names are not specified in the args, we use claude-v1 model by default for all LLM calls. See example logs with GPT-4 over cifar10 [here](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Ozy_zKYdvwcSq3EFnkaudgUXKJmBwQ5t?usp=drive_link).
L00087: 
L00088: # Evaluation
L00089: 
L00090: To run evaluation:
L00091: ```
L00092: python -m MLAgentBench.eval --log-folder <log_folder>  --task <task_name> --output-file <output_name>
L00093: ```
L00094: 
L00095: This will evaluate all runs under <log_folder> as a json.
L00096: 
L00097: To run baseline, run the trivial policy of directly running train.py then submit with ``--agent_type Agent`` as in baseline.sh:
L00098: 
L00099: ```
L00100: python -u -m MLAgentBench.runner --python $(which python) --task cifar10 --device 0 --log-dir first_test  --work-dir workspace --agent_type Agent
L00101: ```
L00102: 
L00103: Finally, to reproduce plots with jsons genereated, run plot.py in MLAgentBench.
L00104: 
L00105: # Workflow
L00106: 
L00107: To run the benchmark systematically, we recommend the following workflow:
L00108: 
L00109: 1. Run parallel experiments over different tasks and different agents using `run_experiments.sh`. This will generate log folders in structure of final_exp_logs/<model_name>/<run_timestamp>/...
L00110: 2. Run baseline.sh on all tasks to provide baselines.
L00111: 2. Run eval.sh with properly specified models and tasks to generate evaluation jsons, including baselines.
L00112: 3. Use plot.py in MLAgentBench to analyze the results. Note you need to fix some paths and names in the file as marked with TODO.
L00113: 
L00114: # Tasks
L00115: 
L00116: Each task is a folder in `MLAgentBench/benchmarks/`, under which the `env/` folder contains files that the research agent will see at the beginning, and `script/` folder contains additional hidden files such as `prepare.py` for downloading data and `eval.py` for evaluation.
L00117: 
L00118: # Agents
L00119: 
L00120: We currently support variants of our research agent along with langchain and autogpt agents. See `run_experiments.sh` for their commands.
L00121: 
L00122: # Results
L00123: Success Rate, i.e. the percentages of runs that achieve more than 10% improvement at the
L00124: last step over the average performance of the baseline in starter code:
L00125: ![](figs/final_improve_10.png)
L00126: 
L00127: 
L00128: 
L00129: Average Improvement over the baseline in starter code among the runs that made a valid
L00130: submission at the last step:
L00131: ![](figs/final_improve.png)
L00132: 
L00133: See all logs here: https://github.com/q-hwang/MLAgentBench_logs
L00134: 
L00135: # Interactive Mode (Under construction)
L00136: 
L00137: You can also specify tasks interactively to the research agent by running `research_agent_interactive.sh`, or ideally as a vscode extension.
L00138:

L00007: def main():
L00008:     requirements_file = sys.argv[1]
L00009:     with open(requirements_file, "r") as f:
L00010:         required_packages = [
L00011:             line.strip().split("#")[0].strip() for line in f.readlines()
L00012:         ]
L00013: 
L00014:     installed_packages = {pkg.key: pkg.version for pkg in pkg_resources.working_set}
L00015: 
L00016:     missing_packages = []
L00017:     for required_package in required_packages:
L00018:         if not required_package:  # Skip empty lines
L00019:             continue
L00020:         pkg = pkg_resources.Requirement.parse(required_package)
L00021:         if (
L00022:             pkg.key not in installed_packages
L00023:             or pkg_resources.parse_version(installed_packages[pkg.key])
L00024:             not in pkg.specifier
L00025:         ):
L00026:             missing_packages.append(str(pkg))
L00027: 
L00028:     if missing_packages:
L00029:         print("Missing packages:")
L00030:         print(", ".join(missing_packages))
L00031:         sys.exit(1)
L00032:     else:
L00033:         print("All packages are installed.")
L00034: 
L00035: 
L00036: if __name__ == "__main__":
L00037:     main()

L00016: """Model base classes and utilities."""
L00017: 
L00018: from typing import Dict, List, Tuple
L00019: import chex
L00020: from clrs._src import probing
L00021: from clrs._src import specs
L00022: import numpy as np
L00023: 
L00024: 
L00025: _Array = chex.Array
L00026: Result = Dict[str, probing.DataPoint]
L00027: 
L00028: 
L00029: def fuse_perm_and_mask(perm: probing.DataPoint,
L00030:                        mask: probing.DataPoint) -> probing.DataPoint:
L00031:   """Replace permutation pointers active in the mask with self-pointers.
L00032: 
L00033:   Args:
L00034:     perm: a node permutation_pointer; data shape is expected to be
L00035:       [..., N, N], and ideally one-hot over the last two dimensions, although
L00036:       this method does not check for one-hotness.
L00037:     mask: a mask_one over nodes; data shape is expected to be
L00038:       [..., N], and ideally one-hot over the last dimension, although
L00039:       this method does not check for one-hotness.
L00040:   Returns:
L00041:     A node pointer with shape [..., N].
L00042:   """
L00043:   assert perm.type_ == specs.Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER
L00044:   assert perm.location == specs.Location.NODE
L00045:   assert mask.name == perm.name + '_mask'
L00046:   assert mask.type_ == specs.Type.MASK_ONE
L00047:   assert mask.location == specs.Location.NODE
L00048:   assert perm.data.shape[-1] == perm.data.shape[-2]
L00049:   assert perm.data.shape[:-1] == mask.data.shape
L00050:   data = np.where(mask.data > 0.5,
L00051:                   np.arange(perm.data.shape[-1]),  # self-pointers
L00052:                   np.argmax(perm.data, axis=-1))   # original pointers
L00053:   return probing.DataPoint(name=perm.name,
L00054:                            type_=specs.Type.POINTER,
L00055:                            location=perm.location,
L00056:                            data=data)
L00057: 
L00058: 
L00059: def _reduce_permutations_tuple(
L00060:     targets: Tuple[probing.DataPoint, ...]) -> Tuple[probing.DataPoint, ...]:
L00061:   """Reduce node pointer + mask_one permutation to just node pointer."""
L00062:   out_targets = []
L00063:   n_perms = 0
L00064:   i = 0
L00065:   while i < len(targets):
L00066:     truth = targets[i]
L00067:     if truth.type_ != specs.Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER:
L00068:       out_targets.append(truth)
L00069:       i += 1
L00070:       continue
L00071:     truth_mask = targets[i + 1]
L00072:     out_targets.append(fuse_perm_and_mask(truth, truth_mask))
L00073:     i += 2
L00074:     n_perms += 1
L00075: 
L00076:   assert len(out_targets) == len(targets) - n_perms
L00077:   return tuple(out_targets)
L00078: 
L00079: 
L00080: def _reduce_permutations_dict(predictions: Result) -> Result:
L00081:   """Reduce node pointer + mask_one permutation to just node pointer."""
L00082:   out_preds = {}
L00083:   n_perms = 0
L00084:   for k, pred in predictions.items():
L00085:     if (k.endswith('_mask') and k[:-5] in predictions and
L00086:         predictions[k[:-5]].type_ == specs.Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER):
L00087:       # This mask will be processed with its associated permutation datapoint
L00088:       continue
L00089:     if pred.type_ != specs.Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER:
L00090:       out_preds[k] = pred
L00091:       continue
L00092:     pred_mask = predictions[k + '_mask']
L00093:     out_preds[k] = fuse_perm_and_mask(pred, pred_mask)
L00094:     n_perms += 1
L00095: 
L00096:   assert len(out_preds) == len(predictions) - n_perms
L00097:   return out_preds
L00098: 
L00099: 
L00100: def evaluate_hints(
L00101:     hints: Tuple[probing.DataPoint, ...],
L00102:     lengths: _Array,
L00103:     hint_preds: List[Result],
L00104: ) -> Dict[str, _Array]:
L00105:   """Evaluate hint predictions."""
L00106:   evals = {}
L00107:   hints = _reduce_permutations_tuple(hints)
L00108:   hint_preds = [_reduce_permutations_dict(h) for h in hint_preds]
L00109:   for truth in hints:
L00110:     assert truth.name in hint_preds[0]
L00111:     eval_along_time = [_evaluate(truth, p[truth.name],
L00112:                                  idx=i+1, lengths=lengths)
L00113:                        for (i, p) in enumerate(hint_preds)]
L00114:     evals[truth.name] = np.sum(
L00115:         [x * np.sum(i+1 < lengths)
L00116:          for i, x in enumerate(eval_along_time)]) / np.sum(lengths - 1)
L00117:     evals[truth.name + '_along_time'] = np.array(eval_along_time)
L00118: 
L00119:   # Unlike outputs, the hints sometimes include scalars, which don't have
L00120:   # a meaningful eval score. So we don't compute a global 'hint score' as we
L00121:   # do for outputs.
L00122:   return evals
L00123: 
L00124: 
L00125: def evaluate(
L00126:     outputs: Tuple[probing.DataPoint, ...],
L00127:     predictions: Result,
L00128: ) -> Dict[str, float]:
L00129:   """Evaluate output predictions."""
L00130:   evals = {}
L00131:   outputs = _reduce_permutations_tuple(outputs)
L00132:   predictions = _reduce_permutations_dict(predictions)
L00133:   for truth in outputs:
L00134:     assert truth.name in predictions
L00135:     pred = predictions[truth.name]
L00136:     evals[truth.name] = _evaluate(truth, pred)
L00137:   # Return a single scalar score that is the mean of all output scores.
L00138:   evals['score'] = sum([v.item() for v in evals.values()]) / len(evals)
L00139:   return evals
L00140: 
L00141: 
L00142: def _evaluate(truth, pred, idx=None, lengths=None):
L00143:   """Evaluate single prediction of hint or output."""
L00144:   assert pred.name == truth.name
L00145:   assert pred.location == truth.location
L00146:   assert pred.type_ == truth.type_
L00147: 
L00148:   if truth.type_ not in _EVAL_FN:
L00149:     raise ValueError('Invalid type')
L00150:   truth_data = truth.data
L00151:   pred_data = pred.data
L00152:   if idx is not None:
L00153:     if np.all(idx >= lengths):
L00154:       return 0.
L00155:     truth_data = truth_data[idx][idx < lengths]
L00156:     pred_data = pred_data[idx < lengths]
L00157:   return _EVAL_FN[truth.type_](pred_data, truth_data)
L00158: 
L00159: 
L00160: def _eval_one(pred, truth):
L00161:   mask = np.all(truth != specs.OutputClass.MASKED, axis=-1)
L00162:   return np.sum(
L00163:       (np.argmax(pred, -1) == np.argmax(truth, -1)) * mask) / np.sum(mask)
L00164: 
L00165: 
L00166: def _mask_fn(pred, truth):
L00167:   """Evaluate outputs of type MASK, and account for any class imbalance."""
L00168:   mask = (truth != specs.OutputClass.MASKED).astype(np.float32)
L00169: 
L00170:   # Use F1 score for the masked outputs to address any imbalance
L00171:   tp = np.sum((((pred > 0.5) * (truth > 0.5)) * 1.0) * mask)
L00172:   fp = np.sum((((pred > 0.5) * (truth < 0.5)) * 1.0) * mask)
L00173:   fn = np.sum((((pred < 0.5) * (truth > 0.5)) * 1.0) * mask)
L00174: 
L00175:   # Protect against division by zero
L00176:   if tp + fp > 0:
L00177:     precision = tp / (tp + fp)
L00178:   else:
L00179:     precision = np.float32(1.0)
L00180:   if tp + fn > 0:
L00181:     recall = tp / (tp + fn)
L00182:   else:
L00183:     recall = np.float32(1.0)
L00184: 
L00185:   if precision + recall > 0.0:
L00186:     f_1 = 2.0 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
L00187:   else:
L00188:     f_1 = np.float32(0.0)
L00189: 
L00190:   return f_1
L00191: 
L00192: _EVAL_FN = {
L00193:     specs.Type.SCALAR:
L00194:         lambda pred, truth: np.mean((pred - truth)**2),
L00195:     specs.Type.MASK: _mask_fn,
L00196:     specs.Type.MASK_ONE:
L00197:         _eval_one,
L00198:     specs.Type.CATEGORICAL:
L00199:         _eval_one,
L00200:     specs.Type.POINTER:
L00201:         lambda pred, truth: np.mean((pred == truth) * 1.0),
L00202: }

L00016: """Unit tests for `evaluation.py`."""
L00017: 
L00018: from absl.testing import absltest
L00019: from clrs._src import evaluation
L00020: from clrs._src import probing
L00021: from clrs._src import specs
L00022: 
L00023: import jax
L00024: import jax.numpy as jnp
L00025: import numpy as np
L00026: 
L00027: 
L00028: class EvaluationTest(absltest.TestCase):
L00029: 
L00030:   def test_reduce_permutations(self):
L00031:     b = 8
L00032:     n = 16
L00033:     pred = jnp.stack([jax.random.permutation(jax.random.PRNGKey(i), n)
L00034:                       for i in range(b)])
L00035:     heads = jax.random.randint(jax.random.PRNGKey(42), (b,), 0, n)
L00036: 
L00037:     perm = probing.DataPoint(name='test',
L00038:                              type_=specs.Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER,
L00039:                              location=specs.Location.NODE,
L00040:                              data=jax.nn.one_hot(pred, n))
L00041:     mask = probing.DataPoint(name='test_mask',
L00042:                              type_=specs.Type.MASK_ONE,
L00043:                              location=specs.Location.NODE,
L00044:                              data=jax.nn.one_hot(heads, n))
L00045:     output = evaluation.fuse_perm_and_mask(perm=perm, mask=mask)
L00046:     expected_output = np.array(pred)
L00047:     expected_output[np.arange(b), heads] = heads
L00048:     self.assertEqual(output.name, 'test')
L00049:     self.assertEqual(output.type_, specs.Type.POINTER)
L00050:     self.assertEqual(output.location, specs.Location.NODE)
L00051:     np.testing.assert_allclose(output.data, expected_output)
L00052: 
L00053: 
L00054: if __name__ == '__main__':
L00055:   absltest.main()
